hero.headline: US launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
Israel launched a new wave of strikes across Tehran shortly after Donald Trump announced he was pausing US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure, signaling what he described as "productive" talks between Washington and Tehran.

The Israeli Defense Forces said it had "just begun another wave of strikes targeting infrastructure of the Iranian terror regime across Tehran," approximately 40 minutes after Trump extended his deadline to strike Iran's power plants by five days. According to al Jazeera Arabic's correspondent in Tehran, the scale of explosions in the Iranian capital was "unprecedented."

Trump said on social media that the US and Iran "have had, over the last two days, very good and productive conversations." He instructed the Department of War to postpone strikes against Iranian power plants and energy infrastructure for five days, pending the success of ongoing negotiations.

An Israeli Defense Forces official told the Times of Israel that the military could not comment on US negotiations with Iran, describing it as a "political echelon matter." The IDF said it was operating according to Israeli government directives and would continue striking until instructed otherwise. However, the IDF also indicated that energy infrastructure would be spared, suggesting Israel may align with Washington in suspending attacks on Iranian power plants.

According to Israeli military statements released Monday, strikes targeted Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps air defense and ground forces headquarters, a Quds Force base and intelligence site, a defense ministry missile production facility, and other research and manufacturing centers. The Guardian could not independently verify these claims.

The human rights group HRANA reported at least 206 attacks across 15 Iranian provinces in the previous 24 hours, resulting in at least four casualties. At least six people were killed in strikes on homes in Tabriz city, according to the Fars news agency.

The Israeli military claimed it had destroyed or disabled approximately 330 of Iran's estimated 470 ballistic missile launchers since the war began. More than half were destroyed in airstrikes, while others were disabled after entrances to underground storage sites were targeted. Missile fire on Israel has declined to about 10 per day recently, down from roughly 90 at the start of the conflict.

Israel has also continued military operations in Lebanon, striking Beirut's southern suburbs on Monday in what the military said was the first attack on the Hezbollah stronghold in several days. Lebanon's health ministry reported one person killed in the strikes.

Israel's far-right finance minister Bezalel Smotrich called Monday for the annexation of areas in southern Lebanon, saying Israel should "apply sovereignty" over areas under its control. He stated the new Israeli border should be the Litani River.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Jump and Stocks Fall After U.S. Shoots Down Iranian Drones
cards.body:
Oil prices rose and stock markets fell after the United States said it shot down four Iranian attack drones. The strikes occurred despite an ongoing ceasefire and peace talks between Washington and Tehran.

The military action cast doubt on the prospects for a peace agreement between the two countries. Oil markets reacted immediately to the news of the confrontation, with investors responding to the heightened risk in the region by moving into oil and away from equities.

The incident marks a significant setback after recent progress in negotiations. Just days earlier, oil prices had tumbled below the $100-a-barrel mark on hopes that the U.S. and Iran were moving closer to a deal. That optimism was quickly reversed by the drone strikes.

The U.S. president had announced he was holding off on threatened attacks on Iran, subject to Tehran agreeing to a two-week ceasefire and reopening the Strait of Hormuz for shipping. Iran's national security council had confirmed it accepted a two-week ceasefire if attacks against Iran were halted. Peace negotiations were set to begin in Islamabad on Friday.

The ceasefire had been welcomed by financial markets. The pan-European Stoxx 600 index had jumped 3.7% in its biggest single-day rise in a year. Wall Street had rallied strongly, with the S&P 500 gaining 2.5% and the Dow Jones industrial average climbing more than 1,300 points. Asian markets had also surged, with Japan's Nikkei 225 gaining more than 5% and South Korea's Kospi soaring by 7.5%.

Oil prices had fallen sharply on ceasefire hopes, with Brent crude dropping 16% and U.S. crude futures sinking 17.6%. Brent crude had reached $94.36 a barrel, heading for its biggest one-day fall since the Covid-19 lockdowns. However, the drone strikes triggered a reversal of those gains.

The incident comes at a sensitive moment in U.S.-Iran relations, with analysts warning that the fragile ceasefire remains vulnerable. Kathleen Brooks, a research director at XTB, noted that markets were watching closely. "Only if the US or Iran walk away from the ceasefire completely and bombing restarts do we see the oil price potentially surging back to the highs of this week above $110 per barrel for Brent crude, which could also cause stocks and bonds to slump," she said.

Jim Reid, a markets strategist at Deutsche Bank, cautioned that investors faced uncertainty ahead. "Will the ceasefire hold? We saw some strikes by Israel and Iran overnight, though these may have been in the works before the conditional ceasefire. We've also seen conflicting commentary on whether the ceasefire will extend to Israel's action in Lebanon."

Investors are now watching to see whether the drone strikes will derail the peace process or prove to be an isolated incident.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations in southern Lebanon as fighting intensifies
cards.teaser: The Israeli military designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and warned of fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has ordered the evacuation of large areas in southern Lebanon, designating regions south of the Zahrani River as combat zones. The military has threatened Hezbollah with fresh strikes in these areas.

The evacuation orders follow intensifying clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Zelensky asks Trump and Congress for Patriot missile interceptors
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian president said his country has not built its own capability to produce anti-missile defense systems.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Wednesday asked President Trump and Congress to provide Patriot missile interceptors to help Ukraine defend against Russian attacks and advance efforts to end the conflict.

Zelensky emphasized that while Ukraine has made progress defending against drone strikes, it lacks the domestic capacity to produce the anti-missile defense systems needed for air defense.

cards.headline: Paper mill implosion in Longview kills at least two, nine missing
cards.teaser: A chemical tank implosion at a Washington state paper mill left at least two people dead and nine missing in what the governor called potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, leaving at least one person dead and nine others missing. Nine additional people were injured in the incident.

The governor warned the disaster could become the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history. White liquor, a caustic chemical used in papermaking, was contained in the ruptured tank.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by President Biden's performance against Donald Trump in the 2024 debate.
cards.body:
In a CBS News interview set to air Sunday, former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's 2024 presidential debate performance against Donald Trump. She stated she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and feared he might have suffered a stroke.

The debate became a pivotal moment in the 2024 election cycle, with Biden's faltering performance drawing significant scrutiny and prompting questions about his fitness to continue his candidacy.

cards.headline: DOJ opens criminal investigation into Trump accuser E. Jean Carroll
cards.body:
The Trump administration has launched a criminal investigation into E. Jean Carroll, the writer who accused President Trump of sexual assault, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times on Wednesday.

Federal prosecutors are examining whether Carroll, 82, committed perjury during a 2022 deposition as part of her civil lawsuits against Trump. The investigation centers on statements Carroll made under oath in which she said she did not receive outside financial support for her legal battles.

Nearly six months after that deposition, Carroll's attorneys informed the judge and Trump's legal team that a nonprofit funded by Reid Hoffman, the billionaire LinkedIn co-founder, had covered some of her legal fees and expenses. Trump's lawyers argued that Carroll had deliberately concealed Hoffman's financial backing, claiming this deception undermined her credibility. Carroll's legal team stated she had never met or spoken with anyone from the nonprofit.

The judge permitted Trump's attorney, Alina Habba, to question Carroll again in a second deposition to address the funding disclosure. However, in 2024, a three-judge federal appeals court panel in New York dismissed the claim that Carroll had lied in her initial deposition.

Carroll, a longtime advice columnist, first made her allegations public in her 2019 book "What Do We Need Men For?" She claimed Trump forced himself upon her in a dressing room at a New York department store in the 1990s. Trump has denied the allegations, stating Carroll was "totally lying" and claiming she was "not my type."

Carroll filed a federal civil lawsuit against Trump for sexual abuse and defamation. A jury found Trump liable on both counts and awarded Carroll 5 million dollars in damages. A separate jury subsequently ordered Trump to pay 83 million dollars in another defamation case. Trump has appealed both judgments.

Todd Blanche, the acting attorney general, has recused himself from the DOJ investigation due to his previous role representing Trump in Carroll's civil cases, according to reports from CNN and the New York Times.

The investigation represents the latest instance of Trump's Justice Department launching criminal probes into political opponents. Federal prosecutors have opened investigations into former FBI director James Comey, New York Attorney General Letitia James, and Democratic members of Congress including Adam Schiff and Ilhan Omar. None of these investigations have resulted in convictions so far.

The Justice Department and Carroll's legal representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the investigation.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing approximately 300 gold bars worth $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former US government official, was arrested after FBI agents discovered the gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush defrauded the government by lying about his credentials in addition to the theft charges.

The case involves one of the largest known thefts of government assets by a former intelligence official. The investigation revealed the extensive cache of gold during a search of Rush's residence. The former CIA officer now faces federal charges related to both the alleged theft and credential fraud.

cards.headline: China Expands Factory Operations Overseas
cards.teaser: Chinese companies are building factories around the world, raising concerns among competitors in those markets.
cards.body:
China is exporting its manufacturing capacity by establishing factories in countries around the world. The expansion has created unease among local competitors in those markets.

The move comes as China manages a $1.2 trillion trade surplus. Some analysts suggest the factory relocations could benefit countries like India as manufacturing spreads beyond Chinese borders.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government has allowed people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout during the war.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after 88 days of censorship that blocked television, chat services, and news for most citizens. The government implemented the near-total shutdown during the three-month war with the United States.

Not everyone in Iran has regained access to the internet. Those who can now connect to the world remain uncertain about how long the restored access will last.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation efforts
cards.teaser: Neither country appears ready to back down months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain locked in open conflict months after Pakistan declared war. China has attempted to mediate between the two countries but neither side has shown willingness to end hostilities.

The fighting continues despite diplomatic efforts by regional powers. The conflict has destabilized the border region between the two countries.

cards.headline: Former federal judges ask court to reopen Trump IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A bipartisan group of former judges petitioned a federal court to investigate a settlement that created a $1.776 billion fund.
cards.body:
A bipartisan group of former federal judges asked a federal court Wednesday to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service. The judges argue that the administration circumvented proper judicial oversight by negotiating a settlement outside the court process.

The Department of Justice announced a $1.776 billion fund in May to compensate alleged "victims of lawfare and weaponization." California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced plans to impose a 100% tax on any payouts received by state residents, seeking to block the distribution of funds to those he views as undeserving recipients.

cards.headline: Trump Accounts App Set to Launch
cards.teaser: A financial app for managing Trump Accounts will become available, ahead of a broader rollout planned for July.
cards.body:
The Trump Accounts mobile app will launch. The app is designed to help users manage Trump Accounts, a new financial system being introduced by the administration.

Treasury Secretary Bessent announced the app would go live. A wider rollout of the Trump Accounts program is scheduled for July 4.

cards.headline: Rivian sets delivery date for first R2 SUVs
cards.teaser: The electric vehicle manufacturer will deliver its first R2 SUVs to customers on June 9.
cards.body:
Rivian will begin delivering the R2 SUV to customers on June 9. CEO RJ Scaringe has described the vehicle as potentially the most important product the company has launched.

The R2 marks Rivian's entry into a new market segment, expanding beyond its existing R1T truck and R1S SUV lineup.

cards.headline: Triomics raises $22 million for cancer center AI tools
cards.teaser: The medical technology company secured Series B funding to develop artificial intelligence systems designed specifically for oncology.
cards.body:
Triomics raised $22 million in a Series B funding round led by Battery Ventures. The company develops artificial intelligence tools specifically designed for cancer centers and oncology applications.

The funding will support the advancement of AI systems tailored to the unique needs of oncology facilities, reflecting Triomics' focus on cancer-specific rather than general-purpose medical AI solutions.

cards.headline: Senators Cruz and Cantwell Introduce Bipartisan College Sports Reform Bill
cards.teaser: Key senators from both parties proposed sweeping college sports legislation that includes salary caps, transfer limits, and enforcement mechanisms.
cards.body:
Senators Ted Cruz and Maria Cantwell introduced bipartisan legislation aimed at reforming college sports. The bill proposes implementing a salary cap for athletes, limiting transfers, and establishing new enforcement protocols for violations.

The proposed legislation also targets coach poaching between programs. SEC leaders are discussing contingency plans as Congress attempts to break a logjam on college sports regulation. The bill represents a significant effort to address eligibility rules and competitive balance in collegiate athletics.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra opens lead in California governor race
cards.teaser: A new poll shows the Health and Human Services Secretary pulling ahead in the crowded Democratic primary to replace Governor Newsom.
cards.body:
Becerra has gained ground in the race as candidates make stops across the state, including recent campaign events in the Bay Area. The election to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom has drawn a packed field of Democratic contenders.

California Democrats have shown mixed reactions to the choices available in the primary. The race has shifted quickly in recent weeks, with multiple candidates competing for position. Voter guides have been published for undecided voters trying to navigate the crowded field as the election approaches.

cards.headline: Senate GOP leaders endorse Ken Paxton after contentious Texas primary
cards.teaser: Republican leadership moved quickly to unite behind the attorney general following his primary victory over Sen. John Cornyn.
cards.body:
Senate Republican leaders are moving to rebuild their relationship with Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton following a contentious primary battle. Senate Majority Leader John Thune spoke with Paxton by phone before publicly endorsing him, signaling to major donors that Republican efforts to maintain Senate control depend on success in Texas.

The gesture marks a shift past the expensive primary contest between Paxton and Senator John Cornyn. Republican leaders are now focused on the general election, with Thune also criticizing the Democratic nominee for the seat.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over $1.2 million Polymarket profit
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly used insider information to profit from trades on a prediction market site.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly used inside information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket trades related to Google Search trends in 2025. According to prosecutors, Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information that gave him knowledge of trading outcomes before the public.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving alleged insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges underscore growing government attention to potential misuse of nonpublic information on these emerging trading sites.

cards.headline: NASA spacecraft captures new images of Mars during flyby
cards.teaser: A NASA probe photographed Mars in high resolution while passing the planet on its journey to study a distant asteroid.
cards.body:
NASA's Psyche spacecraft has transmitted images of Mars captured during a recent flyby of the red planet. The probe photographed Mars while traveling past on its journey to study a metal-rich asteroid.

The images showcase views of Mars' south pole region from a unique vantage point. The Mars flyby provided an unexpected opportunity to gather high-resolution photographs during the spacecraft's transit to its primary mission target.

cards.headline: Georgia Coach Kirby Smart Suggests SEC Could Leave NCAA
cards.teaser: The Georgia head coach said he would support an SEC breakaway from the NCAA to allow the conference to play by its own rules.
cards.body:
Kirby Smart raised the possibility of the SEC leaving the NCAA as expansion arguments intensify in college football. The Georgia coach indicated he would support the conference operating independently and establishing its own rules and governance structure.

Smart's comments hint at potential SEC secession as conference leaders debate the future of college athletics. Some analysts warn that going solo could lead to the death of the SEC, while others see it as a nuclear option the conference is seriously considering to address current competitive and regulatory challenges.

cards.headline: New York and New Jersey Subpoena FIFA Over World Cup Ticket Pricing
cards.teaser: Attorneys general from both states launched an investigation into FIFA's ticket sales practices for the 2026 World Cup.
cards.body:
New York and New Jersey's attorneys general have launched a joint investigation into FIFA's ticketing practices for the 2026 World Cup. The subpoena targets FIFA's sales procedures and pricing structure, with particular focus on matches scheduled at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

The investigation centers on complaints from fans who claim they were misled about seat locations and that FIFA's messaging about tickets contributed to inflated prices throughout the tournament.

cards.headline: Spielberg Opposes AI in Creative Filmmaking Decisions
cards.body:
Steven Spielberg said he opposes using artificial intelligence to make creative decisions in filmmaking during an appearance on Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson's IMO podcast.

The director said AI could be useful for solving medical problems but should not take over the creative process in Hollywood. He drew a line at allowing AI to serve as the final word on creative matters.

Spielberg did not detail specific AI applications he found acceptable in film production or provide examples of uses he opposed. His comments come as the entertainment industry debates how to integrate AI tools while preserving human creativity and employment.

The director's position adds his voice to ongoing discussions about technology's role in filmmaking. Other industry figures have expressed similar concerns about automated systems replacing human judgment in artistic decisions.

Spielberg has directed films including Jaws, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Schindler's List, and Saving Private Ryan over a career spanning five decades. His statements on the podcast represent one of his first public comments on AI in entertainment.

The remarks did not specify whether Spielberg's position applied to all AI uses in film or only certain applications. He also did not address how the industry should regulate or limit AI adoption.

Michelle Obama and Craig Robinson host the IMO podcast, which features conversations on various topics. The full context of Spielberg's comments on the podcast was not provided in available reports.

cards.headline: FIFA Under Investigation for World Cup Ticket Pricing
cards.teaser: New York and New Jersey are investigating FIFA after fans reported being misled about ticket sales and seat locations.
cards.body:
FIFA is being investigated by the attorneys general of New York and New Jersey over World Cup ticket pricing practices. The inquiry was launched after fans reported being misled about ticket sales and seat locations.

Authorities are requiring FIFA to provide explanations regarding the 2026 World Cup ticket sales, examining whether accurate information was given to ticket buyers regarding their purchases and seat assignments.

cards.headline: SEC Leaders Criticize College Football Playoff Metrics Explanation
cards.teaser: Conference officials challenged the CFP's explanation of its ranking criteria as debate over strength of schedule calculations intensifies.
cards.body:
SEC leaders criticized the College Football Playoff committee's explanation of how it evaluates strength of schedule in its ranking metrics. Conference officials expressed frustration with the transparency and methodology used to compare teams from different conferences.

The dispute centers on how the playoff selection committee weighs schedule difficulty when determining which teams qualify for the postseason. SEC leaders argue the current metrics do not adequately reflect the competitive challenges their teams face within the conference.

cards.headline: Ravens Quarterback Lamar Jackson Says Coaching Changes Feel Like Fresh Start
cards.teaser: The Baltimore quarterback called the team's offseason personnel moves a breath of fresh air while declining to discuss contract negotiations.
cards.body:
Lamar Jackson said the Ravens' coaching changes during the offseason feel like a breath of fresh air for the organization. The quarterback discussed his enthusiasm about the new staff while remaining mum on ongoing contract negotiations with the team.

Jackson stated his love for the Ravens has never wavered despite contract discussions. He indicated he wants to leave the conversation about a fully guaranteed contract in the past and focus on the upcoming season with Baltimore's revamped coaching staff.

cards.headline: Box Office Film 'Obsession' Sees Second-Weekend Increase
cards.teaser: The film Obsession increased its box office revenue in its second weekend, a rare occurrence in theatrical releases.
cards.body:
Obsession recorded higher box office earnings in its second weekend of release than its opening weekend. This pattern has not occurred since the film Sound of Freedom.

The film's performance generated attention on TikTok. Director Curry Barker discussed franchising the property and comedic elements in the film. The photography in Obsession also received coverage from photography publications.

cards.headline: ABC News and National Geographic Win Most Awards at News Emmys
cards.teaser: ABC News received eight awards at the 47th News Emmy Awards, with National Geographic earning seven.
cards.body:
ABC News won eight awards at the News Emmy ceremony, including outstanding live news program for ABC World News Tonight With David Muir. The program won the category for the fourth consecutive year.

National Geographic won seven News Emmy awards, primarily for the series Trafficked With Mariana van Zeller. Both ABC News and National Geographic are owned by Disney.

cards.headline: Student Journalist Criticizes CBS News During Scholarship Acceptance Speech
cards.teaser: Santiago Campos, receiving the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship, said CBS News's recent direction stains Mike Wallace's legacy.
cards.body:
The original card text is about Santiago Campos, a student journalist, criticizing CBS News during a scholarship acceptance speech at the News Emmy Awards.

The additional source material is about Sharyn Alfonsi, a 60 Minutes correspondent, accusing CBS News of penalizing her after her contract was not renewed, and involves an editor-in-chief shelving a segment she reported.

These are different stories with different subjects, events, and contexts. Therefore, I'm returning the original card text unchanged:

Santiago Campos, a senior at District of Columbia International School in Washington, D.C., criticized CBS News while accepting the Mike Wallace Memorial Scholarship at the News Emmy Awards. He said the recent direction of the outlet stains the legacy of Mike Wallace.

Former CBS Evening News anchor Scott Pelley presented the scholarship, which is named after the journalist who worked at CBS. Campos's remarks drew attention from the awards audience.

cards.headline: Tipping Practices Spread Beyond United States
cards.teaser: Tipping culture is expanding to other countries as U.S. service workers increasingly expect 20 percent or more.
cards.body:
Tipping practices that originated in the United States are spreading to other countries. American waiting staff have become accustomed to receiving tips of 20 percent or higher, and similar expectations are emerging in other nations.

The shift represents a change in how service workers are compensated internationally. What some describe as out of control tipping culture in the U.S. appears to be influencing practices elsewhere.

cards.headline: Vanilla Ice and Flo Rida to Perform at National Mall Birthday Concert
cards.teaser: Performers including Vanilla Ice, Flo Rida, and Martina McBride will appear at a concert celebrating the country's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
The United States will mark its 250th birthday with a concert on the National Mall. Performers scheduled to appear include Martina McBride, Flo Rida, Vanilla Ice, C+C Music Factory, and Milli Vanilli.

Morris Day and the Time were listed in the lineup, but Day denied rumors of his participation and said it was a no for him. The concert is part of a 16-day patriotic fair called the Great American State Fair scheduled for June in Washington, D.C.

cards.headline: Rodrigo Responds to Criticism of Recent Outfits
cards.teaser: Olivia Rodrigo said people should not be responsible for others sexualizing them after facing backlash over her clothing.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo addressed criticism of her recent outfits, saying people should not be responsible for some guy sexualizing them. Internet commenters accused her recent clothing choices of both infantilizing and sexualizing the singer.

Rodrigo did not specify which outfits prompted the criticism or provide details about the nature of the complaints. The singer has faced ongoing commentary about her fashion choices.

cards.headline: Kanye West Label Executive Sues to Identify Anonymous Website Operator
cards.teaser: Larry Jackson filed a lawsuit seeking to unmask an anonymous figure he says is conducting reputational warfare against him.
cards.body:
Larry Jackson, an executive associated with Kanye West's label, filed a lawsuit asking a judge to help identify an anonymous person. Jackson alleges the individual is operating defamatory websites targeting him.

Jackson described the activity as reputational warfare. The lawsuit seeks to unmask the mystery figure behind the websites. Jackson did not provide details about the content of the websites or the specific allegations they contain.

cards.headline: The Beaches Song Streams Surge After Appearing on TV Show
cards.teaser: The band The Beaches saw streaming of their 2023 song increase 888 percent after it was featured in a scene from Off Campus.
cards.body:
The Beaches experienced significant streaming growth for their 2023 track "Edge of the Earth" following its appearance on the TV show Off Campus. The song was featured in a scene between characters Hannah and Garrett, resulting in an 888 percent increase in streams.

The placement marks another viral moment for the band, demonstrating how television exposure continues to drive listener engagement for their music.

cards.headline: Married at First Sight UK Faces Culture Allegations
cards.teaser: Program insiders describe a focus on sex and toxic culture on the reality show, following rape

cards.headline: Dodgers Place Kike Hernandez Back on Injured List With Oblique Tear
cards.teaser: Los Angeles returned the utility player to the injured list with a significant oblique tear just two games after activating him for the season.

hero.headline: US strikes Iranian military targets for second time in three days
hero.body:
The United States has carried out additional strikes against Iranian military sites, marking the second attack within three days. This military action has occurred during an announced ceasefire period between the two nations, even as diplomatic negotiations continue to address the ongoing three-month conflict.

According to US officials, the strikes targeted attack drones and a drone ground control station located in southern Iran. The American military characterized these operations as defensive measures taken to protect national interests and personnel in the region.

The timing of these strikes has raised questions about the stability of the current ceasefire arrangement. Both countries have publicly described this period as a pause in hostilities, yet military operations have continued throughout. The resumed attacks come as negotiations between US and Iranian representatives are underway to potentially end the broader conflict.

The strikes have had an immediate economic impact, with oil prices rising following news of the military action. Global energy markets remain sensitive to developments in the region, reflecting concerns about potential disruption to supplies and broader Middle East stability.

Despite the ongoing military operations, neither country has provided specific details about the locations targeted or the extent of damage caused. American officials have not disclosed what prompted the defensive action or whether US forces faced imminent threats requiring military response.

The three-month war between the two countries has already created significant disruption to global oil markets and heightened regional tensions. The current diplomatic effort represents the most substantial peace initiative since the conflict began, suggesting both sides maintain some commitment to resolving differences through negotiation.

Throughout the ceasefire period, both the United States and Iran have continued to maintain military forces in the region. The US has justified its military operations by stating they are necessary to safeguard American personnel and strategic interests in the area.

The situation presents a complicated picture of simultaneous military and diplomatic activity. Negotiations are proceeding even as combat operations continue, creating uncertainty about the ceasefire's durability. This pattern of actions raises concerns among observers about whether the two countries can maintain their stated commitment to peace talks while conducting military strikes.

Neither side has indicated a timeline for when negotiations might conclude or provided information about the specific terms being discussed. The lack of transparency about diplomatic progress, combined with continued military action, leaves the status of peace efforts unclear.

The dual approach of negotiating while conducting strikes suggests both nations may be using military demonstrations as leverage in talks. Whether this strategy will ultimately lead to a lasting resolution or further escalation remains uncertain as the situation continues to develop.

cards.headline: Israel orders evacuations in southern Lebanon as fighting intensifies
cards.teaser: The Israeli military designated areas south of the Zahrani River as combat zones and warned of fresh strikes against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel has ordered the evacuation of large areas in southern Lebanon, designating regions south of the Zahrani River as combat zones. The military has threatened Hezbollah with fresh strikes in these areas.

The evacuation orders follow intensifying clashes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah in southern Lebanon.

cards.headline: Iran restores internet access after 88-day shutdown
cards.teaser: The Iranian government has allowed people to reconnect with the world after a near-total internet blackout during the war.
cards.body:
Iran has begun restoring internet access after 88 days of censorship that blocked television, chat services, and news for most citizens. The government implemented the near-total shutdown during the three-month war with the United States.

Not everyone in Iran has regained access to the internet. Those who can now connect to the world remain uncertain about how long the restored access will last.

cards.headline: Australia sues 3M for $2 billion over chemical contamination at defense sites
cards.teaser: The government filed its largest lawsuit ever against the US company over firefighting foam containing forever chemicals.
cards.body:
Australia has launched its largest-ever legal action, suing American manufacturer 3M for more than A$2 billion over contamination at defense bases. The case focuses on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, commonly called "forever chemicals," which were used in firefighting foam at military installations.

Attorney General Michelle Rowland announced the lawsuit against the multinational company over the PFAS contamination. These chemicals do not break down in the environment, raising serious concerns about long-term damage to affected defense sites.

cards.headline: Pakistan and Afghanistan continue fighting despite Chinese mediation efforts
cards.teaser: Neither country appears ready to back down months after Pakistan declared open war on Afghanistan.
cards.body:
Pakistan and Afghanistan remain locked in open conflict months after Pakistan declared war. China has attempted to mediate between the two countries but neither side has shown willingness to end hostilities.

The fighting continues despite diplomatic efforts by regional powers. The conflict has destabilized the border region between the two countries.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared husband was having stroke during 2024 debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance against Donald Trump.
cards.body:
Former first lady Jill Biden told CBS News that she was frightened by Joe Biden's performance during his 2024 presidential debate against Donald Trump. She said she had never seen her husband perform that way before or since, and feared he might have suffered a stroke.

Biden shared her concerns in an interview set to air on CBS News on Sunday. Her comments drew attention to Joe Biden's faltering performance during the televised debate matchup.

cards.headline: Australia charges woman with joining Islamic State after Syria return
cards.teaser: The woman was among several groups who spent years in Syrian camps and returned to Australia in recent months.
cards.body:
Australian authorities have charged a woman with joining Islamic State after she returned from Syria, where she had been held in a camp for years.

Multiple groups of women and children have returned to Australia in recent months after spending extended periods in Syrian camps. These returnees left the camps following the collapse of Islamic State territory in Syria.

cards.headline: Google employee charged with using company data to make $1.2 million on bets
cards.teaser: The longtime worker allegedly broke insider trading laws by using internal information for personal gain.
cards.body:
Federal prosecutors charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud for allegedly using confidential company information to place winning bets on Polymarket, a prediction market platform. Spagnuolo reportedly knew the outcomes of wagers related to search trends before the public did because he had access to Google's internal data.

The case marks the second known criminal prosecution involving someone accused of using insider information to profit on a prediction market site. The charges were filed in New York courts.

cards.headline: Oil prices rise following new US strikes on Iran
cards.teaser: Markets reacted to the military action that occurred during the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran.
cards.body:
The United States launched attacks on Iranian military targets for the second time in three days, striking attack drones and a drone ground-control station in southern Iran. US officials characterized the strikes as self-defense actions.

The attacks occurred during an active ceasefire between the two countries as they negotiate an end to their three-month war. Oil prices jumped in response to the strikes, reflecting market concerns about the stability of the ongoing peace talks and potential disruptions to oil supplies.

hero.headline: US launches second round of strikes on Iran in three days
hero.body:
Israel launched a new wave of strikes across Tehran shortly after Donald Trump announced he was pausing US attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure, signaling what he described as "productive" talks between Washington and Tehran.

The Israeli Defense Forces said it had "just begun another wave of strikes targeting infrastructure of the Iranian terror regime across Tehran," approximately 40 minutes after Trump extended his deadline to strike Iran's power plants by five days. According to al Jazeera Arabic's correspondent in Tehran, the scale of explosions in the Iranian capital was "unprecedented."

Trump said on social media that the US and Iran "have had, over the last two days, very good and productive conversations." He instructed the Department of War to postpone strikes against Iranian power plants and energy infrastructure for five days, pending the success of ongoing negotiations.

An Israeli Defense Forces official told the Times of Israel that the military could not comment on US negotiations with Iran, describing it as a "political echelon matter." The IDF said it was operating according to Israeli government directives and would continue striking until instructed otherwise. However, the IDF also indicated that energy infrastructure would be spared, suggesting Israel may align with Washington in suspending attacks on Iranian power plants.

According to Israeli military statements released Monday, strikes targeted Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps air defense and ground forces headquarters, a Quds Force base and intelligence site, a defense ministry missile production facility, and other research and manufacturing centers. The Guardian could not independently verify these claims.

The human rights group HRANA reported at least 206 attacks across 15 Iranian provinces in the previous 24 hours, resulting in at least four casualties. At least six people were killed in strikes on homes in Tabriz city, according to the Fars news agency.

The Israeli military claimed it had destroyed or disabled approximately 330 of Iran's estimated 470 ballistic missile launchers since the war began. More than half were destroyed in airstrikes, while others were disabled after entrances to underground storage sites were targeted. Missile fire on Israel has declined to about 10 per day recently, down from roughly 90 at the start of the conflict.

Israel has also continued military operations in Lebanon, striking Beirut's southern suburbs on Monday in what the military said was the first attack on the Hezbollah stronghold in several days. Lebanon's health ministry reported one person killed in the strikes.

Israel's far-right finance minister Bezalel Smotrich called Monday for the annexation of areas in southern Lebanon, saying Israel should "apply sovereignty" over areas under its control. He stated the new Israeli border should be the Litani River.

cards.headline: Paper mill implosion in Longview kills at least two, nine missing
cards.teaser: A chemical tank implosion at a Washington state paper mill left at least two people dead and nine missing in what the governor called potentially the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern state history.
cards.body:
A tank ruptured at a paper mill in Longview, Washington, leaving at least one person dead and nine others missing. Nine additional people were injured in the incident.

The governor warned the disaster could become the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history. White liquor, a caustic chemical used in papermaking, was contained in the ruptured tank.

cards.headline: FBI arrests former CIA official with $40 million in gold bars
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors charged a former CIA official with stealing approximately 300 gold bars worth $40 million from the agency.
cards.body:
David Rush, a former US government official, was arrested after FBI agents discovered the gold bars in his home. Prosecutors allege Rush defrauded the government by lying about his credentials in addition to the theft charges.

The case involves one of the largest known thefts of government assets by a former intelligence official. The investigation revealed the extensive cache of gold during a search of Rush's residence. The former CIA officer now faces federal charges related to both the alleged theft and credential fraud.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says she feared Joe Biden was having stroke during debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady told CBS News she was frightened by President Biden's performance against Donald Trump in the 2024 debate.
cards.body:
In a CBS News interview set to air Sunday, former first lady Jill Biden said she was "frightened" while watching her husband's 2024 presidential debate performance against Donald Trump. She stated she had never seen Joe Biden perform that way before or since, and feared he might have suffered a stroke.

The debate became a pivotal moment in the 2024 election cycle, with Biden's faltering performance drawing significant scrutiny and prompting questions about his fitness to continue his candidacy.

cards.headline: Justice Department charges Google employee over $1.2 million Polymarket profit
cards.teaser: Federal prosecutors filed criminal charges against a Google staffer who allegedly used insider information to profit from trades on a prediction market site.
cards.body:
The Justice Department has charged Google employee Michele Spagnuolo with fraud after he allegedly used inside information to profit $1.2 million on Polymarket trades related to Google Search trends in 2025. According to prosecutors, Spagnuolo accessed Google's confidential information that gave him knowledge of trading outcomes before the public.

This marks the second known federal criminal case involving alleged insider trading on a prediction market platform. The charges underscore growing government attention to potential misuse of nonpublic information on these emerging trading sites.

cards.headline: Ken Paxton wins Texas Senate primary in costly race for Republicans
cards.teaser: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton defeated John Cornyn in a Senate primary that cost the party $250 million and shifted the electoral map.
cards.body:
Paxton's victory in the primary came after what media described as a brutal campaign against the longtime senator. Republicans are now working to unite behind Paxton despite the contentious primary battle, with party members attempting to reconcile after the divisive race.

Democratic challenger James Talarico is targeting Paxton's past scandals in the general election race, shifting from the positive message he used during his own primary. The expensive primary has created what analysts call a significant financial hole in the Republican Senate map. National observers are assessing Democratic chances to win the seat in what has traditionally been a Republican stronghold.

cards.headline: Xavier Becerra opens lead in California governor race
cards.teaser: A new poll shows the Health and Human Services Secretary pulling ahead in the crowded Democratic primary to replace Governor Newsom.
cards.body:
Becerra has gained ground in the race as candidates make stops across the state, including recent campaign events in the Bay Area. The election to replace outgoing Governor Gavin Newsom has drawn a packed field of Democratic contenders.

California Democrats have shown mixed reactions to the choices available in the primary. The race has shifted quickly in recent weeks, with multiple candidates competing for position. Voter guides have been published for undecided voters trying to navigate the crowded field as the election approaches.
